calls.head: The Sabres can’t afford to cough it up
calls.body: The Blackhawks turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Sabres are near the bottom of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Sabres.
calls.call: The Blackhawks get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Chicago 8th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Buffalo 26th for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: 6.2% of Chicago’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.6%.

calls.head: One stingy defense, one leaky one
calls.body: On shot suppression, Buffalo is around the middle of the league and Chicago is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Sabres allow fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Blackhawks.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Buffalo had 39.7 per 60 and Chicago 64.1 per 60. Coming in, Buffalo was at 55.2 per 60 and Chicago at 61.7 per 60.

BUF.head: We gave Buffalo a 72% chance, and Buffalo delivered.

CHI.head: We gave Chicago only a 28% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Chicago tried a different line
surprises.body: F. Nazar, P. Kane, R. Kantserov played 13:56 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Chicago’s usual lines.

surprises.head: Chicago shut down Buffalo’s power play
surprises.body: Buffalo’s power play created 3.1 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.3 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 10 games.

story.head: The Sabres come back from two down
paras: Ryan Donato opened the scoring midway through the first. Four different Sabres scored. The Blackhawks led by two, but the Sabres came all the way back. Jiri Kulich scored the winner late in the third.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Sabres win about four in five. By our Swing measure, Alex Vlasic had the best night of anyone, even in a loss. The Blackhawks tried a line they hadn’t used before: Frank Nazar, Patrick Kane and Roman Kantserov.
